title: Caseous necrosis as a pathology word
dek: Cheese-like dead tissue in granulomas. Wikipedia's histopathology term. Lesion PK and hypoxia stay on tb-caseum.
story: Caseous necrosis is Wikipedia's name for the crumbly, acellular, lipid-rich dead zone classically sitting in tuberculous granulomas. Pathologists say caseation; pharmacologists say caseum. This card is the dictionary cross-walk.
The clinic plates already treat caseum as hypoxic, acidic, drug-hostile, and full of slowly replicating bacilli. Do not re-derive PZA and rifamycin lesion PK from the encyclopedia photo caption.
Caseation is not unique to TB (some fungi, some other mycobacteria), so the word is a pattern, not a species call.
deep: Liquefaction toward an airway is how a caseous center becomes a cavity — transmission plate territory.
Mouse models that do not caseate are the wrong PK classroom; that sentence already lives on tb-granuloma.
Do not dose from a histopathology page.
Ghon calcification can follow caseation; that is sequence, not sterility.
